title: Finding a Place
description: Ask for a destination and follow an integrated set of simple directions.
objectives: Ask for a destination and follow an integrated set of simple directions.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to ask for a destination and follow an integrated set of simple directions. The central language is integrated town and direction review. It belongs to the practical context of home & around town. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the finding a place exchange.

blocks.english: Go straight and it's on your right.
blocks.explanation: This finding a place model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the finding a place exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?” and “Go straight and it's on your right.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: integrated town and direction review.
